title: Geometric Patterns: Shape Patterns, Tables and Rules
seo_title: Grade 5 Geometric Patterns Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Investigate and extend geometric patterns looking for relationships or rules of patterns represented in physical or diagram form: sequences involving a constant difference or ratio, and of the learner's own creation; describe the general rules for the observed relationships; determine input values, output values and rules for the patterns and relationships using flow diagrams and tables.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 5 geometric patterns worksheets: growing shape patterns, pattern tables, rules and later figures. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Figure number → rule → number of objects.
key_sub: Test the rule on the first figures.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • In a growing shape pattern, each figure adds the same number of objects.
  • Make a table of the figure number and the number of objects.
  • Find the rule: figure 1 has 5, figure 2 has 8, figure 3 has 11. The rule is figure number × 3 + 2.
  • Use the rule to find figure 20 without drawing it: 20 × 3 + 2 = 62.

Examples

Example

Matches: 4, 7, 10, …

+ 3 each figure

rule: × 3 + 1

Answer: figure 10 has 31 matches

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The figure beforeUse the figure number in the question.
Forgetting the start× 3 + 1, not just × 3.
Wrong stepFind what is added each time.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 5 say about geometric patterns?
faq.a: Investigate and extend geometric patterns represented in physical or diagram form, with a constant difference or ratio, describe the rules, and use flow diagrams and tables.
So you can find any figure without drawing them all.
Yes, n can stand for the figure number.
The same number added each time.

items.q:
What is the next term?
6, 10, 14, 18, ?
items.e: The pattern grows by 4 each time (6 + 4 = 10). Next: 18 + 4 = 22.

items.q:
What is the next term?
15, 23, 31, 39, ?
items.e: The pattern grows by 8 each time (15 + 8 = 23). Next: 39 + 8 = 47.
The pattern grows by 2 500 each time (12 500 + 2 500 = 15 000). Next: 20 000 + 2 500 = 22 500.

items.q:
What is the next term?
120, 145, 170, 195, ?
items.e: The pattern grows by 25 each time (120 + 25 = 145). Next: 195 + 25 = 220.

items.q:
What is the next term?
1 000, 875, 750, 625, ?
items.e: The pattern shrinks by 125 each time (1 000 − 125 = 875). Next: 625 − 125 = 500.

items.q:
What is the next term?
90, 84, 78, 72, ?
items.e: The pattern shrinks by 6 each time (90 − 6 = 84). Next: 72 − 6 = 66.

items.q:
What is the next term?
75, 70, 65, 60, ?
items.e: The pattern shrinks by 5 each time (75 − 5 = 70). Next: 60 − 5 = 55.

items.q:
What is the next term?
150, 138, 126, 114, ?
items.e: The pattern shrinks by 12 each time (150 − 12 = 138). Next: 114 − 12 = 102.

items.q:
What is the next term?
2, 6, 18, 54, ?
items.e: Each term is 3 times the one before: 54 × 3 = 162. (Adding the first jump, 54 + 4 = 58, only works for the first step.)

items.q:
What is the next term?
1, 2, 4, 7, 11, ?
items.e: The jumps are 1, 2, 3, 4, so the next jump is 5: 11 + 5 = 16. (Adding the first jump gives 12.)

items.q:
What is the next term?
3, 6, 12, 24, ?
items.e: The jumps are 3, 6, 12, so the pattern does not add the same amount. Each term is 2 times the one before: 24 × 2 = 48. (Adding the first jump, 24 + 3 = 27, only works for the first step.)

items.q:
What is the next term?
640, 320, 160, 80, ?
items.e: Each term is half of the one before (divide by 2): 80 ÷ 2 = 40. (Subtracting 320 like the first step does not work after that.)

items.q:
What is the missing term?
4 500, 5 000, 5 500, ?, 6 500
items.e: The pattern grows by 500 each time. The missing term is 5 500 + 500 = 6 000. Check: 6 000 + 500 = 6 500.

items.q:
What is the missing term?
35, 50, ?, 80, 95
items.e: The pattern grows by 15 each time. The missing term is 50 + 15 = 65. Check: 65 + 15 = 80.

items.q:
What is the missing term?
8, ?, 20, 26, 32
items.e: The pattern grows by 6 each time. The missing term is 8 + 6 = 14. Check: 14 + 6 = 20. (The jump from 8 to 20 is 12, but the missing term sits halfway between them.)

items.q:
What is the missing term?
100, 92, ?, 76, 68
items.e: The pattern shrinks by 8 each time. The missing term is 92 − 8 = 84. Check: 84 − 8 = 76.

items.q: The pattern continues. How many tiles will Figure 4 need?
items.e: Count each figure: 3, 5, 7. Each figure adds 2 tiles. Figure 4: 7 + 2 = 9.

items.q: The pattern continues. How many craft sticks will Figure 4 need?
items.e: Count each figure: 4, 7, 10. Each figure adds 3 craft sticks. Figure 4: 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: The pattern continues. How many craft sticks will Figure 4 need?
items.e: Count each figure: 6, 11, 16. Each figure adds 5 craft sticks. Figure 4: 16 + 5 = 21.

items.q: The pattern continues. How many tiles will Figure 4 need?
items.e: Count each figure: 4, 6, 8. Each figure adds 2 tiles. Figure 4: 8 + 2 = 10.

items.q: The pattern rule is □ × 5 + 3, where □ is the term number. What is the term value for term number 7?
items.e: Put 7 in the box: 7 × 5 + 3 = 35 + 3 = 38. Multiply first, then add. (Adding 3 before multiplying gives 50.)

items.q: The pattern rule is □ × 4 + 2, where □ is the term number. What is the term value for term number 6?
items.e: Put 6 in the box: 6 × 4 + 2 = 24 + 2 = 26. Multiply first, then add. (Adding 2 before multiplying gives 32.)

items.q: The pattern rule is □ × 6 − 2, where □ is the term number. What is the term value for term number 9?
items.e: Put 9 in the box: 9 × 6 − 2 = 54 − 2 = 52. Multiply first, then subtract. (Subtracting 2 before multiplying gives 42.)

items.q: The pattern rule is □ × 2 + 9, where □ is the term number. What is the term value for term number 12?
items.e: Put 12 in the box: 12 × 2 + 9 = 24 + 9 = 33. Multiply first, then add. (Adding 9 before multiplying gives 42.)

items.q: The pattern rule is □ × 3 + 1, where □ is the term number. What is the term value for term number 8?
items.e: Put 8 in the box: 8 × 3 + 1 = 24 + 1 = 25. Multiply first, then add. (Adding 1 before multiplying gives 27.)

items.q: Which rule gives the term value? (□ is the term number.)
items.e: The term value goes up by 5, so the rule has □ × 5. Term 1: 1 × 5 = 5, and the value is 3, so subtract 2. Check term 4: 4 × 5 − 2 = 18. (A rule must work for every term, not only term 1.)

items.q: Which rule gives the term value? (□ is the term number.)
items.e: The term value goes up by 4, so the rule has □ × 4. Term 1: 1 × 4 = 4, and the value is 7, so add 3. Check term 4: 4 × 4 + 3 = 19. (A rule must work for every term, not only term 1.)

items.q: Which rule gives the term value? (□ is the term number.)
items.e: The term value goes up by 2, so the rule has □ × 2. Term 1: 1 × 2 = 2, and the value is 7, so add 5. Check term 4: 4 × 2 + 5 = 13. (A rule must work for every term, not only term 1.)

items.q: Which rule gives the term value? (□ is the term number.)
items.e: The term value goes up by 3, so the rule has □ × 3. Term 1: 1 × 3 = 3, and the value is 5, so add 2. Check term 4: 4 × 3 + 2 = 14. (A rule must work for every term, not only term 1.)

items.q: Which rule gives the term value? (□ is the term number.)
items.e: The term value goes up by 6, so the rule has □ × 6. Term 1: 1 × 6 = 6, and the value is 10, so add 4. Check term 4: 4 × 6 + 4 = 28. (A rule must work for every term, not only term 1.)

items.q: Which rule gives the number of craft sticks in Figure □?
items.e: The counts are 6, 11, 16: each figure adds 5 craft sticks, so the rule has □ × 5. Figure 1: 1 × 5 + 1 = 6. Check Figure 3: 3 × 5 + 1 = 16.

items.q: Which rule gives the number of craft sticks in Figure □?
items.e: The counts are 4, 7, 10: each figure adds 3 craft sticks, so the rule has □ × 3. Figure 1: 1 × 3 + 1 = 4. Check Figure 3: 3 × 3 + 1 = 10.

items.q: Which rule gives the number of tiles in Figure □?
items.e: The counts are 5, 9, 13: each figure adds 4 tiles, so the rule has □ × 4. Figure 1: 1 × 4 + 1 = 5. Check Figure 3: 3 × 4 + 1 = 13.

items.q: Which rule gives the number of tiles in Figure □?
items.e: The counts are 3, 5, 7: each figure adds 2 tiles, so the rule has □ × 2. Figure 1: 1 × 2 + 1 = 3. Check Figure 3: 3 × 2 + 1 = 7.

items.q: Which rule gives the number of tiles in Figure □?
items.e: The counts are 4, 6, 8: each figure adds 2 tiles, so the rule has □ × 2. Figure 1: 1 × 2 + 2 = 4. Check Figure 3: 3 × 2 + 2 = 8.

items.q: The pattern rule is □ × 5 + 5, where □ is the term number. Which term number has a term value of 60?
items.e: Work backwards. Undo + 5: 60 − 5 = 55. Undo × 5: 55 ÷ 5 = 11. Check: 11 × 5 + 5 = 60. (60 is the term value, not the term number.)

items.q: The pattern rule is □ × 4 − 4, where □ is the term number. Which term number has a term value of 36?
items.e: Work backwards. Undo − 4: 36 + 4 = 40. Undo × 4: 40 ÷ 4 = 10. Check: 10 × 4 − 4 = 36. (36 is the term value, not the term number.)

items.q: The pattern rule is □ × 3 + 3, where □ is the term number. Which term number has a term value of 33?
items.e: Work backwards. Undo + 3: 33 − 3 = 30. Undo × 3: 30 ÷ 3 = 10. Check: 10 × 3 + 3 = 33. (33 is the term value, not the term number.)

items.q: The pattern rule is □ × 10 + 20, where □ is the term number. Which term number has a term value of 150?
items.e: Work backwards. Undo + 20: 150 − 20 = 130. Undo × 10: 130 ÷ 10 = 13. Check: 13 × 10 + 20 = 150. (150 is the term value, not the term number.)

items.q: The pattern rule is □ × 2 + 4, where □ is the term number. Which term number has a term value of 30?
items.e: Work backwards. Undo + 4: 30 − 4 = 26. Undo × 2: 26 ÷ 2 = 13. Check: 13 × 2 + 4 = 30. (30 is the term value, not the term number.)

items.q: The rule for a pattern is 3n + 1, where n is the term number. What is the term value when n = 7?
items.e: 3n means 3 × n. 3 × 7 = 21, then 21 + 1 = 22. (3n is not the number 37.)

items.q: The rule for a pattern is 2n + 7, where n is the term number. What is the term value when n = 8?
items.e: 2n means 2 × n. 2 × 8 = 16, then 16 + 7 = 23. (2n is not the number 28.)

items.q: The rule for a pattern is 5n + 2, where n is the term number. What is the term value when n = 10?
items.e: 5n means 5 × n. 5 × 10 = 50, then 50 + 2 = 52. (5n is not the number 510.)

items.q: The rule for a pattern is 4n − 3, where n is the term number. What is the term value when n = 9?
items.e: 4n means 4 × n. 4 × 9 = 36, then 36 − 3 = 33. (4n is not the number 49.)

items.q: The rule for a pattern is 6n − 4, where n is the term number. What is the term value when n = 5?
items.e: 6n means 6 × n. 6 × 5 = 30, then 30 − 4 = 26. (6n is not the number 65.)

items.q: Which list shows the first four terms of the pattern 3n + 2? (n = 1, 2, 3, 4)
items.e: Put each term number in the rule. n = 1: 3 × 1 + 2 = 5. n = 2: 3 × 2 + 2 = 8. The terms go up by 3. (2, 5, 8, 11 starts at n = 0; 6, 7, 8, 9 reads 3n as 3 + n.)

items.q: Which list shows the first four terms of the pattern 30 − 3n? (n = 1, 2, 3, 4)
items.e: n = 1: 30 − 3 × 1 = 27. n = 2: 30 − 3 × 2 = 24. The terms go down by 3: 27, 24, 21, 18. (30 is not a term, because n starts at 1.)

items.q: Which list shows the first four terms of the pattern 2n + 5? (n = 1, 2, 3, 4)
items.e: Put each term number in the rule. n = 1: 2 × 1 + 5 = 7. n = 2: 2 × 2 + 5 = 9. The terms go up by 2. (5, 7, 9, 11 starts at n = 0; 8, 9, 10, 11 reads 2n as 2 + n.)

items.q: Which list shows the first four terms of the pattern 10n + 4? (n = 1, 2, 3, 4)
items.e: Put each term number in the rule. n = 1: 10 × 1 + 4 = 14. n = 2: 10 × 2 + 4 = 24. The terms go up by 10. (4, 14, 24, 34 starts at n = 0; 15, 16, 17, 18 reads 10n as 10 + n.)

items.q: Which list shows the first four terms of the pattern 5n + 1? (n = 1, 2, 3, 4)
items.e: Put each term number in the rule. n = 1: 5 × 1 + 1 = 6. n = 2: 5 × 2 + 1 = 11. The terms go up by 5. (1, 6, 11, 16 starts at n = 0; 7, 8, 9, 10 reads 5n as 5 + n.)

items.q: Which rule gives the term value? (n is the term number.)
items.e: The value goes up by 4, so the rule has 4n. For n = 1, 4n is 4 and the value is 5, so add 1: 4n + 1. Check n = 4: 4 × 4 + 1 = 17. (A rule must work for every term.)

items.q: Which rule gives the term value? (n is the term number.)
items.e: The value goes up by 2, so the rule has 2n. For n = 1, 2n is 2 and the value is 8, so add 6: 2n + 6. Check n = 4: 2 × 4 + 6 = 14. (A rule must work for every term.)

items.q: Which rule gives the term value? (n is the term number.)
items.e: The value goes up by 3, so the rule has 3n. For n = 1, 3n is 3 and the value is 7, so add 4: 3n + 4. Check n = 4: 3 × 4 + 4 = 16. (A rule must work for every term.)

items.q: Which rule gives the term value? (n is the term number.)
items.e: The value goes down by 4, so the rule subtracts 4n. For n = 1: 50 + 4 = 54, so the rule is 54 − 4n. Check n = 4: 54 − 16 = 38. (50 − 4n gives 46 for n = 1.)

items.q: Which rule gives the term value? (n is the term number.)
items.e: The value goes up by 10, so the rule has 10n. For n = 1, 10n is 10 and the value is 5, so subtract 5: 10n − 5. Check n = 4: 10 × 4 − 5 = 35. (A rule must work for every term.)

items.q: The rule for a pattern is 2n + 6, where n is the term number. Which term number has a term value of 40?
items.e: Find n so that 2n + 6 = 40. Undo + 6: 40 − 6 = 34. Undo × 2: 34 ÷ 2 = 17. So n = 17. (40 is the term value, not the term number.)

items.q: The rule for a pattern is 4n + 8, where n is the term number. Which term number has a term value of 64?
items.e: Find n so that 4n + 8 = 64. Undo + 8: 64 − 8 = 56. Undo × 4: 56 ÷ 4 = 14. So n = 14. (64 is the term value, not the term number.)

items.q: The rule for a pattern is 3n + 6, where n is the term number. Which term number has a term value of 51?
items.e: Find n so that 3n + 6 = 51. Undo + 6: 51 − 6 = 45. Undo × 3: 45 ÷ 3 = 15. So n = 15. (51 is the term value, not the term number.)

items.q: The rule for a pattern is 7n − 7, where n is the term number. Which term number has a term value of 63?
items.e: Find n so that 7n − 7 = 63. Undo − 7: 63 + 7 = 70. Undo × 7: 70 ÷ 7 = 10. So n = 10. (63 is the term value, not the term number.)

items.q: The rule for a pattern is 6n + 12, where n is the term number. Which term number has a term value of 90?
items.e: Find n so that 6n + 12 = 90. Undo + 12: 90 − 12 = 78. Undo × 6: 78 ÷ 6 = 13. So n = 13. (90 is the term value, not the term number.)

items.q: Compare each B term with the A term in the same column. Which is true for every pair of corresponding terms?
items.e: Look down each column: 3 × 2 = 6, 6 × 2 = 12, 9 × 2 = 18. Each B term is 2 times the A term. (“B is 3 more than A” works only for 3 and 6: 12 is 6 more than 6.)

items.q: Compare each B term with the A term in the same column. Which is true for every pair of corresponding terms?
items.e: Look down each column: 2 × 4 = 8, 4 × 4 = 16, 6 × 4 = 24. Each B term is 4 times the A term. (“B is 6 more than A” works only for 2 and 8: 16 is 12 more than 4.)

items.q: Compare each B term with the A term in the same column. Which is true for every pair of corresponding terms?
items.e: Look down each column: 5 × 3 = 15, 10 × 3 = 30, 15 × 3 = 45. Each B term is 3 times the A term. (“B is 10 more than A” works only for 5 and 15: 30 is 20 more than 10.)

items.q: Compare each B term with the A term in the same column. Which is true for every pair of corresponding terms?
items.e: Look down each column: 4 × 5 = 20, 8 × 5 = 40, 12 × 5 = 60. Each B term is 5 times the A term. (“B is 16 more than A” works only for 4 and 20: 40 is 32 more than 8.)

items.q: Compare each B term with the A term in the same column. Which is true for every pair of corresponding terms?
items.e: Look down each column: 6 × 2 = 12, 12 × 2 = 24, 18 × 2 = 36. Each B term is 2 times the A term. (“B is 6 more than A” works only for 6 and 12: 24 is 12 more than 12.)

items.q: Compare each B term with the A term in the same column. Which is true for every pair of corresponding terms?
items.e: Look down each column: 7 × 3 = 21, 14 × 3 = 42, 21 × 3 = 63. Each B term is 3 times the A term. (“B is 14 more than A” works only for 7 and 21: 42 is 28 more than 14.)

items.q: Compare each B term with the A term in the same column. Which is true for every pair of corresponding terms?
items.e: Look down each column: 0 + 4 = 4, 3 + 4 = 7, 6 + 4 = 10. Each B term is 4 more than the A term. The rule Add 3 tells how each pattern grows, not how A and B compare.

items.q: Compare each B term with the A term in the same column. Which is true for every pair of corresponding terms?
items.e: Look down each column: 1 + 6 = 7, 6 + 6 = 12, 11 + 6 = 17. Each B term is 6 more than the A term. The rule Add 5 tells how each pattern grows, not how A and B compare.

items.q: Pattern A: start at 0, Add 3. Pattern B: start at 0, Add 6. Why is each B term 2 times the A term?
c: B always adds 3 more than A
B starts at a bigger number
items.e: Both patterns start at 0. Each step, B adds 6 and A adds 3, and 6 = 2 × 3. After any number of steps, B has added 2 times as much as A, so B is 2 times A: for example 4 × 3 = 12 and 4 × 6 = 24.

items.q: Pattern A: start at 0, Add 5. Pattern B: start at 4, Add 5. Why is each B term always 4 more than the A term?
c: Both add 5, and B starts 4 higher
items.e: B starts 4 higher (4 − 0 = 4). Each step both patterns add the same number, 5, so the difference never changes: 0 and 4, 5 and 9, 10 and 14.

items.q: Ordered pairs are written (A term, B term). Which ordered pair is made from corresponding terms?
items.e: 6 is the 3rd term of A and 12 is the 3rd term of B, so they correspond. Write the A term first: (6, 12). (12, 6) has the numbers switched.

items.q: Ordered pairs are written (A term, B term). Which ordered pair is made from corresponding terms?
items.e: 6 is the 4th term of A and 30 is the 4th term of B, so they correspond. Write the A term first: (6, 30). (30, 6) has the numbers switched.

items.q: Ordered pairs are written (A term, B term). Which ordered pair is made from corresponding terms?
items.e: 4 is the 2nd term of A and 12 is the 2nd term of B, so they correspond. Write the A term first: (4, 12). (12, 4) has the numbers switched.

items.q: Ordered pairs are written (A term, B term). Which ordered pair is made from corresponding terms?
items.e: 15 is the 4th term of A and 60 is the 4th term of B, so they correspond. Write the A term first: (15, 60). (60, 15) has the numbers switched.

items.q: Ordered pairs are written (A term, B term). Which ordered pair is made from corresponding terms?
items.e: 5 is the 3rd term of A and 8 is the 3rd term of B, so they correspond. Write the A term first: (5, 8). (8, 5) has the numbers switched.

items.q: Ordered pairs are written (A term, B term). Which ordered pair is made from corresponding terms?
items.e: 200 is the 3rd term of A and 600 is the 3rd term of B, so they correspond. Write the A term first: (200, 600). (600, 200) has the numbers switched.

items.q: These ordered pairs come from two patterns: (0, 0), (2, 6), (4, 12), (6, 18), ? Which ordered pair comes next?
items.e: The first numbers go up by 2 and the second numbers go up by 6. After (6, 18) comes (6 + 2, 18 + 6) = (8, 24).

items.q: These ordered pairs come from two patterns: (0, 0), (4, 8), (8, 16), (12, 24), ? Which ordered pair comes next?
items.e: The first numbers go up by 4 and the second numbers go up by 8. After (12, 24) comes (12 + 4, 24 + 8) = (16, 32).

items.q: These ordered pairs come from two patterns: (0, 0), (5, 20), (10, 40), (15, 60), ? Which ordered pair comes next?
items.e: The first numbers go up by 5 and the second numbers go up by 20. After (15, 60) comes (15 + 5, 60 + 20) = (20, 80).

items.q: These ordered pairs come from two patterns: (0, 0), (1, 3), (2, 6), (3, 9), ? Which ordered pair comes next?
items.e: The first numbers go up by 1 and the second numbers go up by 3. After (3, 9) comes (3 + 1, 9 + 3) = (4, 12).

items.q: Sarah’s bean plant grows the same amount each day. How tall will it be on day 8?
items.e: It grows 3 cm a day. From day 1 to day 8 there are 7 jumps: 2 + 7 × 3 = 23 cm. (14 cm is day 5, the next point.)

items.q: Andile builds a row of triangles with toothpicks. 1 triangle uses 3, 2 triangles use 5 and 3 triangles use 7. How many toothpicks does he need for 15 triangles?
items.e: Each new triangle adds 2 toothpicks. From 1 to 15 triangles there are 14 jumps: 3 + 14 × 2 = 31. (15 × 3 = 45 counts the shared sides twice.)

items.q: Thabo makes a row of squares with craft sticks: 4 sticks, 7 sticks, 10 sticks, … Which figure uses 31 sticks?
items.e: The sticks go up by 3. 31 − 4 = 27, and 27 ÷ 3 = 9 jumps after Figure 1, so it is Figure 10. (31 is the number of sticks, not the figure number.)

items.q: Square tables are pushed together in a row for a class party. 1 table seats 4 learners, 2 tables seat 6, and 3 tables seat 8. How many learners can sit at 10 tables?
items.e: Each new table adds 2 seats. From 1 table to 10 tables there are 9 jumps: 4 + 9 × 2 = 22. (10 × 4 = 40 counts seats lost where the tables touch.)

items.q: Today is Monday. Days of the week repeat every 7 days. What day of the week will it be 30 days from today?
items.e: 30 ÷ 7 = 4 R 2. After 4 full weeks (28 days) it is Monday again. 2 more days: Wednesday.

items.q: Each point is (day, height). Which point will come next on the graph?
items.e: The next day is day 5. The height goes up 3 cm: 11 + 3 = 14. The point is (5, 14). (In (14, 5) the numbers are swapped: the day comes first.)

items.q: The graph shows the pages Lerato has left to read in her book at the end of each day. Which pattern rule matches the graph?
c: Start at 25 and subtract 10 each day.
Start at 25 and add 5 each day.
Start at 25 and subtract 5 each day.
Start at 30 and subtract 5 each day.
items.e: The first point is 25, and each point is 5 lower: 25, 20, 15, 10. So start at 25 and subtract 5 each day.

items.q: How many triangles will Figure 4 have?
items.e: Each figure has 2 triangles more than the one before (1, 3, 5). Figure 4: 5 + 2 = 7.

items.q: How many toothpicks will Figure 4 have?
items.e: Each figure has 3 toothpicks more than the one before (4, 7, 10). Figure 4: 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: How many squares will Figure 4 have?
items.e: Each figure has 2 squares more than the one before (3, 5, 7). Figure 4: 7 + 2 = 9.

items.q: How many squares will Figure 4 have?
items.e: Each figure has 4 squares more than the one before (5, 9, 13). Figure 4: 13 + 4 = 17.

items.q: How many dots will Figure 4 have?
items.e: Each figure has 2 dots more than the one before (4, 6, 8). Figure 4: 8 + 2 = 10.

items.q: Which rule tells how the pattern grows?
items.e: Each figure has 2 squares more than the one before (7, 9, 11). The rule is Add 2. Figure 1 is only the start: 7 is not the rule.

items.q: Which rule tells how the pattern grows?
items.e: Each figure has 2 triangles more than the one before (1, 3, 5). The rule is Add 2. Figure 1 is only the start: 1 is not the rule.

items.q: Which rule tells how the pattern grows?
items.e: Each figure has 4 squares more than the one before (9, 13, 17). The rule is Add 4. Figure 1 is only the start: 9 is not the rule.

items.q: Which rule tells how the pattern grows?
items.e: Each figure has 2 toothpicks more than the one before (3, 5, 7). The rule is Add 2. Figure 1 is only the start: 3 is not the rule.

items.q: Which rule tells how the pattern grows?
items.e: Each figure has 4 dots more than the one before (4, 8, 12). The rule is Add 4.

items.q: How many squares will Figure 6 have?
items.e: Each figure has 3 squares more than the one before (6, 9, 12). From Figure 1 to Figure 6 there are 5 jumps of 3: 6 + 5 × 3 = 21.

items.q: How many triangles will Figure 7 have?
items.e: Each figure has 2 triangles more than the one before (3, 5, 7). From Figure 1 to Figure 7 there are 6 jumps of 2: 3 + 6 × 2 = 15.

items.q: How many squares will Figure 8 have?
items.e: Each figure has 4 squares more than the one before (5, 9, 13). From Figure 1 to Figure 8 there are 7 jumps of 4: 5 + 7 × 4 = 33.
